To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a prime/boost vaccine that uses a vector and a protein boost is effective against cancer in young and old animals, even when the animals are immunosuppressed.

the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd-CD40L vector induces a potent T cell and Ab response to the TAA and to the Annexn A1 vascular Ag in both young and old mice, and that this response is further increased with a TAA protein boost, which may be valuable for reducing postsurgical recurrence of a variety of epithelioma.

the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd CD40L prime-TAA/CD40L protein vaccine boost platform can be used to induce a tumor suppressive CD4 T cell response to the h MUC-1 and Annexin A1 TAAs in old mice, and that it can also be used to reduce postsurgery recurrence of epithelial cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel vaccines that can overcome the immune defects associated with aging and cancer and can induce a potent tumor suppressive immune responses.
developing novel cancer immunotherapeutic strategies to treat postsurgery recurrence in breast cancer.
the development of novel vaccines for the treatment of human cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd-CD40L vector and TAA/ecd- CD40L protein vaccine platform induces a tumor-suppressive immune response to the TAA and to the tumor vascular Ag, in young and old mice, and that the vaccine is capable of overcoming the defects acquired in the aged immune system and in cancer.

our Ad-sig-TTA/ecdCD40-L vector prime-TAA/protein boost vaccine platform has the ability to overcome the defects acquired by aging and cancer and to generate an effective tumor-specific immune response in both young and old mice.

the Ad-sg-TAA/ecd-CD40L vector vaccine platform induces tumor-specific CD8 T-cell and Ab responses in mice with anergic T cells and that this vaccine platform is a potential candidate to prevent the recurrence of breast and ovarian cancer in women with a history of these cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd-CD40L vector vaccine induces a potent tumor-specific immune response in mice.

we have shown that the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd CD40L vector prime/ecdCD40 protein boost vaccine platform induces an anti-tumor immune response to the TAA hMUC- 1, rH2N, and Annexin A1, and that the TAA/CD40L protein vaccine boost is more effective than the Ad-sig- TAA/CD4OPL vector prime alone, in both 2- and 18-mo old mice.

the Ad-sigs-TAA/ecdC40L vector prime-protein boost vaccination strategy is an efficient and effective approach that can induce tumor suppressive immune responses to TAAs, even in aged animals, which have anergy to these Ags, and in animals in which cancer has developed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that it is possible to overcome the defects in the aging immune system, and even the immune system of cancer-bearing mice, with a vector protein boost vaccine platform.
the Ad-sigsig-TAA/cedCD40L vector and TAA/cedCD4O protein vaccine can overcome the immunological defects associated with aging and cancer.
the Ad-sigma-TAA/ecd-CD40L vector and the TAA/CD40L protein vaccine can induce a strong anti-TAA immune response in young and old mice.
